bio_en: Ghazar Petoyan, known as Keri Ghazar or Peto Ghazar, was born about 1880 in Geliguzan in Sasun into the house of Peto, the most influential family of the Shatakh district of Sasun, whose home sheltered revolutionaries. A shepherd until 1894, he went in late 1894 to study at the Arakelots monastery, which he left when the 1904 Sasun uprising broke out; in that fighting he saw Semal burn, Sebouh wounded and his leader Hrayr killed. After a period in Adana and Constantinople from 1908, he worked in the Talvorik area until 1914 and survived the 1915 struggle, surrendering with about 250 villagers to the Russians after they took Mush in February 1916. Later, in Soviet Armenia, he was arrested by the Cheka after the 1925 Khushoyan affair, escaped to the mountains and settled in Maghda village in the Talin district.
